text:
kai_support: FYI — production customer reporting large bill spike + 500s today. They say our Node client started 404ing on chat create and client code kept retrying.
maria_eng: Can you paste the exact error and the client version they're using?
kai_support: Error from their logs:
```
Error: Route not found: chat.create
    at Request.handleResponse (/opt/app/node_modules/@redwood/client/lib/request.js:78:15)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues:95:5)
```
They're on `@redwood/client@0.22.0` and calling `client.chat.create({ messages: [...] })`.
ashley_support: Thanks — does our API currently expect a different route name or param casing? Could be the v0.23 rename we shipped.
maria_eng: Looks like it — in 0.23 we moved to `client.createChat()` and changed param `messages` -> `input` (server route `chat.create` -> `create_chat`). 0.22 maps to the old API surface. If they updated the hosted API to the new route but kept the older client, mismatch happens.
kai_support: Customer says they only upgraded the server side (api) via terraform module and left the client pinned. They got a sequence of retries from our SDK (default 5 retries) — that multiplied token usage and spiked billing.
tim_oncall: Repro on my laptop: using 0.22 against current hosted API returns 404 for `chat.create` and SDK retries. Repro snippet:
```
const c = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
await c.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-1', messages: [{role:'user', content:'hi'}] })
// => 404 Route not found, then automatic exponential retries
```
maria_eng: Action items: (1) immediate mitigation: update docs and send customer a workaround; (2) short-term patch: make server accept both `chat.create` and `create_chat` for a grace period; (3) longer: improve SDK/server compatibility checks and add warning header when route aliasing occurs.
ashley_support: Workaround I gave customer: pin server to older API by setting `api_compat: v0.22` in their config, or upgrade their client to `@redwood/client@0.23.1`. Also told them to reduce SDK retries by setting `retries: 1` in the client constructor to limit cost while they migrate.
maria_eng: Can we add a short-term server-side shim ASAP? I can open a PR to accept both route names and return a `X-RW-Incompatibility: shimmed` header so we can track how many customers hit it.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: merge request #5123 by maria_eng — will roll out to staging in 10m.
kai_support: Customer acknowledged workaround and reduced traffic. They've asked for an incident report and cost credit evaluation.
maria_eng: I'll follow up with a postmortem draft once the shim is deployed and we have metrics on how many calls were retried. Suggest we also add a compatibility endpoint at `GET /_compat` that returns the supported client versions to help clients detect mismatches.
ashley_support: I'll open the billing ticket and tag legal for credits if their usage exceeds threshold due to our incompatibility.
kai_support: Thanks — keeping thread updated. Main lessons: pinning server/client compatibility in release notes + clearer deprecation window. :thumbsup:
